v1/common.proto

Top

Engine

Engine is the database engine of an instance. Only the engines the product

actually supports are kept: MySQL-compatible ones (MySQL, TiDB, MariaDB,

OceanBase, StarRocks, Doris), PostgreSQL and SQL Server. The other removed

values keep their numbers reserved so they can never be silently reused for

something else.

NameNumberDescription
ENGINE_UNSPECIFIED 0

MSSQL 1

MYSQL 2

POSTGRES 3

TIDB 6

MARIADB 13

OCEANBASE 14

STARROCKS 15

DORIS 16

State

NameNumberDescription
STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0

ACTIVE 1

DELETED 2

v1/application_service.proto

Top

Application

Application is one application whose statements are reported to the workspace.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

The resource name. Format: applications/{application_id}

application_id string

The stable identifier, equal to the last segment of `name`.

display_name string

The display name. It is unique: it is how a person names the application.

description string

disabled bool

A stopped application keeps every row it ever reported, and none of its keys report anything any more.

created_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

updated_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

ApplicationAPIKey

ApplicationAPIKey is one reporting credential. Only its masked form is ever returned

after creation.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

The resource name. Format: applications/{application_id}/apiKeys/{api_key}

api_key_id string

masked_key string

The masked key, safe to display.

description string

created_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

last_used_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

The last request this key was used for, and how many it has made.

request_count int64

Per-key counters. They stand in for one audit row per request: the audit ledger is kept forever, so auditing machine traffic would grow it with request volume rather than with distinct statements.

statement_accepted_count int64

Statements rather than reports: a report whose entry carried a script counts once per statement in it.

statement_rejected_count int64

ApplicationSQL

ApplicationSQL is one distinct statement an application reported, with every literal

already replaced by `?`.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
guid string

The globally unique metadata GUID.

application_sql_id string

instance_resource_id string

database_name string

schema_name string

engine Engine

sql_text string

The parameterized statement. This is the only form ever stored.

kind ApplicationSQLKind

fingerprint string

The fingerprint that identifies the statement within its scope, and the version of the rules that produced it.

fingerprint_version int32

execution_count int64

How many times every application ran it, and when it was first and last seen.

first_seen_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

last_seen_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

observations ApplicationSQLObservation repeated

The applications that reported it, with each one's own history.

ApplicationSQLObservation

ApplicationSQLObservation is one application's own history with one statement.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
application string

application_display_name string

execution_count int64

first_seen_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

last_seen_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

The maximum number of API keys to return. If unspecified, at most 50 are returned. The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000.

ApplicationSQLKind

ApplicationSQLEngineKind is the read/write classification of a statement.

NameNumberDescription
APPLICATION_SQL_KIND_UNSPECIFIED 0

APPLICATION_SQL_KIND_UNKNOWN 1

Not analyzed yet: the runner writes the classification after it analyzes the statement.
APPLICATION_SQL_KIND_READ 2

APPLICATION_SQL_KIND_WRITE 3

ApplicationService

ApplicationService manages the applications that report the SQL they run, and the

statements they have reported.

An application is deliberately not a metadata resource: it has no schema, no columns and

no lineage of its own. Creating one issues its first API key, which is the credential the

reporting endpoint authenticates; the key names the application, so a report cannot claim

to be another one.

Lists reported statements. The parent scopes the result to one instance and database.
GetApplicationSQL GetApplicationSQLRequest ApplicationSQL

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
Login LoginRequest LoginResponse

Permissions required: None
Logout LogoutRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Permissions required: None
Refresh RefreshRequest RefreshResponse

Refresh rotates the web session: it consumes the refresh-token cookie and sets a new access token and a new refresh token cookie. It needs no credential because it is called exactly when the access token has expired, and it rotates the pair so a stolen refresh token is worthless once the real holder refreshes. Permissions required: None
ExchangeRefreshToken ExchangeRefreshTokenRequest ExchangeRefreshTokenResponse

ExchangeRefreshToken rotates a CLI session from the refresh token in the body. The CLI has no cookie jar, so it presents the opaque refresh token the device login issued instead of the browser's cookie; the session itself is the same rotating grant row an MCP client gets, which is what makes a CLI login a visible, revocable connected app. Each call consumes the presented token and returns a replacement, so a stolen copy is worthless once the real holder refreshes. Permissions required: None
CreateSSOState .google.protobuf.Empty CreateSSOStateResponse

CreateSSOState issues a one-time OAuth2 state value. A client must fetch it before redirecting to the identity provider, pass it back to the provider and then send it with the login request; the server consumes it there. Without it an attacker can complete an authorization-code flow in a victim's browser and bind the victim's session to the attacker's identity. Permissions required: None
CreateDeviceLogin CreateDeviceLoginRequest CreateDeviceLoginResponse

CreateDeviceLogin starts a device login (RFC 8628 style). The caller gets a polling secret plus a short human-readable code; a signed-in user approves the request from the web confirmation page and the CLI then exchanges the secret for an access token bound to that user. Permissions required: None
GetDeviceLogin GetDeviceLoginRequest DeviceLogin

GetDeviceLogin returns one pending device login so the confirmation page can show what is being approved. Permissions required: None
ApproveDeviceLogin ApproveDeviceLoginRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

ApproveDeviceLogin approves or denies a pending device login. The approver becomes the identity the access token is issued for. Permissions required: None
ExchangeDeviceLogin ExchangeDeviceLoginRequest ExchangeDeviceLoginResponse

ExchangeDeviceLogin polls a device login. An approved request is consumed and answered with the token; every other state is reported as-is. Permissions required: None

v1/connected_app_service.proto

Top

ConnectedApp

ConnectedApp is one user's authorization of one client: an MCP client through

the OAuth browser flow, or the `mxd` CLI through a device login. Both are the

same rotating grant record, so both are listed, revocable and labeled here; the

kind field says which ceremony produced the row. It is derived from that record,

not from the client registration: the same client may be authorized several

times, and each authorization is its own row.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

The resource name of the connected app, in the form `connectedApps/{id}`.

client_id string

The client identifier: a dynamic registration's identifier (RFC 7591) for an MCP client, or the built-in `mxd` client for a CLI session. Opaque.

client_name string

The client's self-reported name at registration. It is not verified, so it is display text only. A CLI row shows the built-in client's name.

user string

The user whose identity the client acts as, in the form `users/{id}`.

user_email string

The user's email. It is filled only for the caller's own rows or when the caller may read users; a connected-apps reader is not thereby a user reader.

resource string

The MCP resource identifier the authorization was granted for. Empty for a CLI session, which is not bound to the MCP endpoint and is refused there because its access token carries the user API audience.

scopes string repeated

The OAuth scopes the user consented to. Empty for a CLI session.

create_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

When the authorization completed (the first token pair was issued).

last_tool_call_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

The most recent tool call made with an MCP connection. Empty for a client that has not called a tool yet and for a CLI session, whose activity is not a tool call.

expire_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

When the refresh credential expires. A connection past this instant cannot mint another access token. The lifetime slides on every rotation, so an actively used connection keeps moving this instant out.

state ConnectedApp.State

The connection's current state.

revoke_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

When the connection was revoked. Set only for REVOKED.

kind ConnectedApp.Kind

Which authorization ceremony created the connection.

client_version string

The CLI build that created the session, e.g. "0.1.0" (display only; empty for an MCP connection).

request_ip string

The source address the CLI device login came from, as the server resolved it (trusted-proxy rules applied; empty for an MCP connection). It is personal data, so it lives only as long as the grant row.

ListConnectedAppsRequest

FieldTypeLabelDescription
page_size int32

The maximum number of connected apps to return. The service may return fewer than this value. If unspecified, at most 50 are returned. The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 are coerced to 1000.

page_token string

A page token, received from a previous `ListConnectedApps` call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. The filter and user parameters must not change between pages.

user string

The user whose connected apps to list, in the form `users/{id}`. Omitted, a caller holding metaxisdata.connectedApps.list sees every connection in the workspace, and any other caller sees only their own. Naming another user is refused unless the caller holds that permission.

filter string

A CEL filter over the list. Supported variables: user == "users/{id}" state == "ACTIVE" | "REVOKED" | "EXPIRED" | "REAUTH_REQUIRED" | "INACTIVE" client == "name" (exact), client.matches("substring") client_id == "id" (exact), client_id.matches("substring") user_email == "email" (exact), user_email.matches("substring") create_time >= / <= RFC 3339 The filter only narrows the rows the caller is already allowed to see.

ListConnectedAppsResponse

FieldTypeLabelDescription
connected_apps ConnectedApp repeated

The connected apps on this page.

next_page_token string

A token, which can be sent as `page_token` to retrieve the next page. If this field is omitted, there are no subsequent pages.

RevokeConnectedAppRequest

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

The resource name of the connected app to revoke, in the form `connectedApps/{id}`.

ConnectedApp.Kind

Kind is what produced the grant. Both kinds rotate and revoke identically;

only the authorization ceremony and the token audience differ.

NameNumberDescription
KIND_UNSPECIFIED 0

MCP 1

Authorized through the OAuth browser flow (authorization code + PKCE).
CLI 2

Authorized through a CLI device login.

ConnectedApp.State

State is a derived value: it is computed from the stored grant, the MCP

surface's current configuration, and the user's account, so it is not stored.

NameNumberDescription
STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0

ACTIVE 1

Usable: not revoked or expired, and a refresh would be accepted.
REVOKED 2

Explicitly revoked. Outstanding access tokens are refused within the revocation cache's window.
EXPIRED 3

The refresh credential expired; no new access token can be minted.
REAUTH_REQUIRED 4

Re-authorization is required before the connection can work: the MCP resource identifier changed (MCP only), or the grant predates the user's last password change.
INACTIVE 5

The user's account is deactivated. The connection resumes if the account is restored; it is not revoked automatically.

ConnectedAppService

ConnectedAppService manages the connections a user established by authorizing

a client against this deployment: an MCP client through the OAuth browser flow,

or the `mxd` CLI through a device login. One connected app is one authorization

(one user, one client, one ceremony), not one transport session: the MCP

endpoint itself is stateless, and a CLI session is the rotating grant behind its

stored tokens.

No method here carries a (metaxisdata.v1.permission) annotation, because the

same call serves two audiences: a workspace administrator listing every

connection and an ordinary user managing their own. Each handler therefore

scopes its query and authorizes the widen itself, the way NotificationService

and UserService's self-service paths do. The permission catalog still defines

connectedApps.list and connectedApps.revoke, which are what the handler checks

before returning another user's rows or revoking another user's connection.

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
ListConnectedApps ListConnectedAppsRequest ListConnectedAppsResponse

List the caller's connected apps. A caller holding metaxisdata.connectedApps.list sees the whole workspace; without it the result is forced to the caller's own rows. `user` narrows the result further when the caller may see other users' connections.
RevokeConnectedApp RevokeConnectedAppRequest ConnectedApp

Revoke one connected app: its outstanding access tokens stop being accepted (immediately on this replica, within 30 seconds elsewhere, the same rule as Logout) and its refresh token can no longer mint a new pair. A user may revoke their own; revoking another user's needs metaxisdata.connectedApps.revoke. The response is the revoked record so the permanent audit ledger names what was revoked even after the row is pruned. Permissions required: None

Whether the sync also refreshes every existing database of the instance. Unset means true: a user-triggered sync refreshes the metadata and every database, which is what the background scan and instance creation already do. Set it to false only for a discovery-only sync that refreshes the instance metadata and queues the databases that were just discovered, leaving the existing ones to the background scan.

ApplicationSQLMetadata

ApplicationSQLMetadata is one statement an application reported, with every literal

already replaced by `?`. It is the metadata browser's view of the object; how often it

ran and which applications reported it are on the Application SQL page, because the

registry row is written once and those numbers change with every report.

ColumnMetadata

ColumnMetadata is the metadata for columns.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

The name of the column.

position int32

The position is the position in columns.

default string

The default value of the column.

default_on_null bool

Oracle specific metadata. The default_on_null is the default on null of a column.

on_update string

The on_update is the on update action of a column. For MySQL like databases, it's only supported for TIMESTAMP columns with CURRENT_TIMESTAMP as on update value.

nullable bool

The nullable is the nullable of a column.

type string

The type is the type of a column.

character_set string

The character_set is the character_set of a column.

collation string

The collation is the collation of a column.

comment string

The comment is the comment of a column. classification and user_comment is parsed from the comment.

user_comment string

The user_comment is the user comment of a table parsed from the comment.

generation GenerationMetadata

The generation is for generated columns.

is_identity bool

identity_generation ColumnMetadata.IdentityGeneration

The identity_generation is for identity columns, PG only.

identity_seed int64

The identity_seed is for identity columns, MSSQL only.

identity_increment int64

The identity_increment is for identity columns, MSSQL only.

default_constraint_name string

The default_constraint_name is the name of the default constraint, MSSQL only. In MSSQL, default values are implemented as named constraints. When modifying or dropping a column's default value, you must reference the constraint by name. This field stores the actual constraint name from the database. Example: A column definition like: CREATE TABLE employees ( status NVARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active' ) Will create a constraint with an auto-generated name like 'DF__employees__statu__3B75D760' or a user-defined name if specified: ALTER TABLE employees ADD CONSTRAINT DF_employees_status DEFAULT 'active' FOR status To modify the default, you must first drop the existing constraint by name: ALTER TABLE employees DROP CONSTRAINT DF__employees__statu__3B75D760 ALTER TABLE employees ADD CONSTRAINT DF_employees_status DEFAULT 'inactive' FOR status This field is populated when syncing from the database. When empty (e.g., when parsing from SQL files), the system cannot automatically drop the constraint.

ListDatabasesRequest

FieldTypeLabelDescription
parent string

- workspaces/-: list databases in the workspace. - instances/{instances}: list databases in a instance.

page_size int32

The maximum number of databases to return. The service may return fewer than this value. If unspecified, at most 10 databases will be returned. The maximum value is 1000; values above 1000 will be coerced to 1000.

page_token string

A page token, received from a previous `ListDatabases` call. Provide this to retrieve the subsequent page. When paginating, all other parameters provided to `ListDatabases` must match the call that provided the page token.

filter string

Filter is used to filter databases returned in the list. The syntax and semantics of CEL are documented at https://github.com/google/cel-spec Supported filter: - environment: the environment full name in "environments/{id}" format, support "==" operator. - name: the database name, support ".matches()" operator. - instance: the instance full name in "instances/{id}" format, support "==" operator. - engine: the database engine, check Engine enum for values. Support "==", "in [xx]", "!(in [xx])" operator. - drifted: should be "true" or "false", show drifted databases if it's true, support "==" operator. - labels.{key}: the database label, support "==" and "in" operators. For example: environment == "environments/{environment resource id}" environment == "" (find databases which environment is not set) instance == "instances/{instance resource id}" name.matches("database name") engine == "MYSQL" engine in ["MYSQL", "POSTGRES"] !(engine in ["MYSQL", "POSTGRES"]) drifted == true labels.environment == "production" labels.region == "asia" labels.region in ["asia", "europe"] You can combine filter conditions like: environment == "environments/prod" && name.matches("employee")

show_deleted bool

Show deleted database if specified.

databases Database repeated

All database name list.

next_page_token string

A token, which can be sent as `page_token` to retrieve the next page. If this field is omitted, there are no subsequent pages.

https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/clustered-indexes/#clustered-indexes CLUSTERED or NONCLUSTERED.

TablePartitionMetadata

TablePartitionMetadata is the metadata for table partitions.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

The name of the table partition.

type TablePartitionMetadata.Type

The type of a table partition.

expression string

The expression is the expression of a table partition. For PostgreSQL, the expression is the text of {FOR VALUES partition_bound_spec}, see https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createtable.html. For MySQL, the expression is the `expr` or `column_list` of the following syntax. PARTITION BY { [LINEAR] HASH(expr) | [LINEAR] KEY [ALGORITHM={1 | 2}] (column_list) | RANGE{(expr) | COLUMNS(column_list)} | LIST{(expr) | COLUMNS(column_list)} }.

value string

The value is the value of a table partition. For MySQL, the value is for RANGE and LIST partition types, - For a RANGE partition, it contains the value set in the partition's VALUES LESS THAN clause, which can be either an integer or MAXVALUE. - For a LIST partition, this column contains the values defined in the partition's VALUES IN clause, which is a list of comma-separated integer values. - For others, it's an empty string.

use_default string

The use_default is whether the users use the default partition, it stores the different value for different database engines. For MySQL, it's [INT] type, 0 means not use default partition, otherwise, it's equals to number in syntax [SUB]PARTITION {number}.

subpartitions TablePartitionMetadata repeated

The subpartitions is the list of subpartitions in a table partition.

indexes IndexMetadata repeated

check_constraints CheckConstraintMetadata repeated

exclude_constraints ExcludeConstraintMetadata repeated

FieldTypeLabelDescription

The bounding box. (SQL Server specific).

grid_levels GridLevel repeated

The grid levels. (SQL Server specific).

cells_per_object int32

The number of cells per object. (SQL Server specific).

AcceptedValuesConfig

AcceptedValuesConfig counts rows whose column value is outside the accepted

set. The set comes from exactly one source: the fixed list, another column of

the same target, or a single-column query.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
column string

values string repeated

At most 200 values, encoded as strings and converted by the column's type.

allow_null bool

When false (the default), a NULL value is a violation.

fail_threshold double optional

warn_threshold double optional

field string

A column of the same target whose distinct values are the accepted set. Mutually exclusive with values and query.

query AcceptedValuesQuery

A query whose values are the accepted set. Mutually exclusive with values and field. The reference side is read over the target's own read-only data source, so it may name another database or schema of that instance but not another instance.

AcceptedValuesQuery

AcceptedValuesQuery is the accepted set a single-column query returns.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
sql string

One SELECT or WITH statement of at most 8 KiB. It is parsed before it runs; time variables are rendered the same way a custom SQL check renders them.

value_column string

The column the query returns. Named explicitly because the server tests it for NULL (a NULL in the set would make NOT IN unknown for every row).

ColumnValue is one column of a sampled failed row. Values are truncated before

they are returned, so a wide text column cannot bloat the response.

FieldTypeLabelDescription

The value rendered as display text. Empty for a SQL NULL and for an empty string; is_null tells the two apart.

Whether the value was SQL NULL. A sample recorded before this field existed has no marker, and its NULLs are indistinguishable from empty strings.

When set, the rule's target is taken from the suggestion: a request target that names a different target is rejected rather than silently ignored, so a caller cannot create a rule for one table while accepting another table's draft. The suggestion is marked accepted once the rule exists. A decision that cannot be written does not roll the created rule back; it is logged and the suggestion can be decided explicitly.

Re-propose drafts that were already accepted or rejected, and re-analyze columns that already have a fact. The queue is still deduplicated by identity: regeneration refreshes a pending proposal instead of appending a duplicate.

CrossTableConfig

CrossTableConfig reconciles one aggregate of the rule's table with one

aggregate of a reference relation, which may live in another database or

another instance. A reference in the target's own database is read in the

same statement as the target side; anything else is read over its own

read-only connection.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
left_function QualityAggregateFunction

The left (target) aggregate; COUNT ignores left_column.

left_column string

right_function QualityAggregateFunction

The right (reference) aggregate; COUNT ignores right_column.

right_column string

tolerance double optional

The absolute difference tolerated before the thresholds apply: the observed value is max(0, |left - right| - tolerance).

fail_threshold double optional

Difference beyond the tolerance that fails, and the warning level inside it. The fail threshold defaults to zero.

warn_threshold double optional

reference CrossTableReference

The reference relation; required.

right_filter QualityFilter

Rows the reference side reads, bounded like the rule's own filter. The rule's filter and the target contract's filter never apply to the reference side; this is the only filter it sees.

CrossTableReference

CrossTableReference names the relation a reconciliation compares against, as

a registry target. Unlike a table name it can point at any database and

instance of the workspace.

ExportQualityDataChunk

ExportQualityDataChunk is one slice of a streamed CSV export. A client

concatenates the slices into a file: the first slice starts with a UTF-8 BOM

and the header row, so the file opens cleanly in a spreadsheet without a

manual encoding choice.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
data bytes

A slice of the CSV bytes. A slice may end in the middle of a value's UTF-8 sequence; the document is only meaningful once every slice is concatenated.

row_count int64

The total number of data rows written so far, across all slices. It is monotonic and the last value is the export's row count, which lets a client report progress without counting the document.

truncated bool

Whether max_rows cut the export short: the document is complete as a CSV file, but it does not hold the whole selection. Set on the final slice only.

GetQualityTargetImpactRequest

FieldTypeLabelDescription
parent string

Format: workspaces/{workspace}. "workspaces/-" is the current workspace.

target QualityTargetKey

The target whose impact to read. The target does not have to be monitored or to still resolve: lineage recorded before it disappeared is still walked.

depth int32

How many lineage levels downstream to walk, 0-3. Zero means two; a larger value is coerced to three. The upstream walk behind the root causes is always two levels.

as_of google.protobuf.Timestamp

The instant the root-cause window ends: the start of the failure being explained. Zero means now; a value in the future is read as now.

window_hours int32

How far back root-cause evidence is looked for, in hours 0-168. Zero means 24; a larger value is coerced to 168.

GetQualityTargetImpactResponse

FieldTypeLabelDescription
downstream_assets QualityImpactAsset repeated

The assets the target's data reaches downstream, nearest first. Only the object types a check can watch are listed; a reported statement, an external dataset or an object that no longer exists is walked through but counted in omitted_downstream_count instead.

root_causes QualityRootCauseCandidate repeated

Upstream targets with root-cause evidence inside the window, strongest first: a target with failing checks outranks one whose structure changed, then the nearer one wins, then the more recent evidence.

depth_reached int32

The largest distance a downstream asset was found at; 0 when nothing is recorded downstream.

downstream_truncated bool

Whether the node or time budget cut the downstream walk short.

omitted_downstream_count int32

How many walked downstream objects are not listed as assets. A floor when downstream_truncated is true.

upstream_truncated bool

Whether the two-level upstream walk was cut short by its node budget.

omitted_root_cause_count int32

How many root-cause candidates were found beyond the twenty returned.

window_start google.protobuf.Timestamp

The window the root causes were read from: [window_start, window_end].

window_end google.protobuf.Timestamp

QualityAction

QualityAction is one card of the WS2 action catalog with its live policy verdict.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
id string

The stable catalog id, e.g. "A0-4" or "A3-1".

title string

A short developer-facing title; the UI owns the localized copy.

autonomy_level string

A0 (read/propose), A1 (reversible action), A2 (changes future judging) or A3 (changes promises, responsibility or irreversible state).

actor string

AGENT or HUMAN: who may ever perform it.

red_line bool

A red line never accepts a pure model proposal, even with autonomy on.

implemented bool

False when this codebase has no write path for the action yet; such an action is refused with its own reason instead of pretending to work.

agent_reachable bool

Whether the shipped agent role and handlers actually expose the action to an agent. It differs from implemented on purpose: a person may author a check while an agent can only propose it through a change request.

agent_allowed bool

Whether an enabled agent would be allowed to do it under the current policy.

requires_approval bool

Whether a person must still approve the action after the policy allows it.

decision_code string

The machine-readable verdict: ALLOWED, DENIED_AUTONOMY_OFF, DENIED_HUMAN_ONLY, DENIED_RED_LINE, DENIED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, DENIED_NOT_EXPOSED, DENIED_CRITICAL, DENIED_UNKNOWN_ACTOR or REQUIRES_APPROVAL (allowed as a proposal that a person must still approve).

reason string

QualityContract

QualityContract is the target-level layer above the rules: defaults, the

published version and whether the live rules have drifted from it. It is a

projection, not a second source of truth: editing a rule changes the live

contract immediately, and publishing records that state as a version.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
target QualityTarget

settings QualityContractSettings

published_version int32

The newest published version; 0 means the target has never been published.

published_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

published_by string

Format: users/{user}. Empty when the publisher is unknown.

publish_note string

check_count int32

How many live (non-archived) rules the target has.

change_summary QualityContractChangeSummary

The live rules compared with the published snapshot. Zero counts when the target has never been published.

has_unpublished_changes bool

True when the live rules or settings differ from the published snapshot (or nothing has been published yet and the target has content).

plan QualityPlan

The target's monitoring plan as derived from the live rules and the contract.

staged_plan QualityPlan

The plan declaration the target currently holds, published or not. Absent when the target has none; an empty declaration clears it and returns the target to the projection derived from the intent and the live rules.

staged_base_version int32

The newest published version the declaration is aligned to. It always equals published_version after a publish, so a client echoes it back as the base of its next declaration edit.

diff QualityContractDiff

How the working state (the draft when one exists, otherwise the live projection) differs from the newest published version.

QualityContractChangeSummary

QualityContractChangeSummary counts how the live rules differ from the

published snapshot.

FieldTypeLabelDescription

modified int32

removed int32

sections the version's plan payload made comparable.

True when the newest published version predates the plan payload, so a plan diff cannot be shown. It is not the same as "no plan changes".

QualityContractIntent is the target's declaration above the checks: its

criticality, the properties it commits to, its dependents and the requirements

it explicitly waived. Editing it is part of UpdateQualityContract, and it is

versioned with the contract on every publish.

When the declaration is meant to take effect; unset means unset. Recorded only: plan derivation does not evaluate it yet.

QualityExecution

QualityExecution is one rule checked once: the durable unit of the data

quality engine. A scheduled tick or a manual request plans one execution per

rule; the runner then executes it and records the verdict and its evidence on

the same row.

FieldTypeLabelDescription

The target as it was when the execution was planned.

The quality verdict: PASS, WARN, FAIL, ERROR, SKIPPED or NOT_EVALUATED. Unset while the execution is PENDING or RUNNING; an ABANDONED execution never produced one.

The principal that asked for the execution. Format: users/{user}. Empty for a scheduled execution.

The instance the target lives in. Format: instances/{instance}

The thresholds that were applied, snapshotted.

True when the observation was made over a sample rather than every row.

sample_rows int64

True when the samples were cut off by the sample limit.

Failed rows kept as evidence, already truncated per value.

executed_sql string

The SQL that was executed. Kept so an execution can be re-checked by hand.

A machine-readable failure class: CONNECTION, AUTH, TIMEOUT, PERMISSION, UNSUPPORTED, SQL_SYNTAX, BAD_DATA, LIMIT_EXCEEDED or ORPHANED. Empty unless outcome is ERROR.

A human-readable failure message. Empty unless outcome is ERROR.

finish_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

Unset while the execution is PENDING or RUNNING.

The dispatch batch that planned this execution, so the execution directory can group checks by the run that produced them. Format: workspaces/{workspace}/qualityRuns/{quality_run}

attempt int32

The scheduled attempt number in the target's current due cycle: 1 for the first attempt, 2+ for a retry after an abandoned attempt. Manual executions always use 1. A retry is planned only while the attempt budget lasts.

baseline_value double optional

The row count a row_count_change check compared against. Unset for every other type, and for a first observation that had no recent baseline to compare with; the verdict then follows on_empty, which a new count-change check defaults to PASS so the first run only records the baseline.

baseline_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

When that baseline was measured. Unset whenever baseline_value is.

reference_executed_sql string

The statement that read a reconciliation's reference side, when the reference needed its own connection. Empty for every other execution and for a reconciliation whose two sides share the target's connection.

passing_samples FailureSample repeated

Rows that passed the same check, kept beside the failed rows so a reviewer can compare the two populations. Only the row-level check types whose passing rows are a row predicate keep them, and only when the verdict was WARN or FAIL (a passing verdict has no failed rows to compare against).

segment_evidence SegmentObservation

The segment set a segment check observed, compared with its baseline. Unset for every other check type.

QualityRuleSampling

QualityRuleSampling bounds how much of the target one execution reads. The two

methods are user intents: "read a share of the rows" and "read at most this

many rows". The editor only offers the methods the target engine can express,

and the server refuses one it cannot, so a check never silently degrades to a

different sample.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
max_rows int64

Read at most this many rows of the filtered relation. Every engine can express it, and the read cost is bounded; the rows are an arbitrary prefix, so the sample is not random.

percent double

Read approximately this percent (1-99) of the relation. The engine's own sampling clause decides the exact behavior; it is approximately random, and its cost depends on the engine.

QualitySuggestionQueueSummary is what one generation pass did to the review

skipped_columns string repeated

The columns a generation pass derived no proposal for, so the client can name them. A label pass lists columns it left out because they already had a label or a live proposal; a deterministic recommendation lists columns no check could be derived for. A column whose candidate lost the pass's per-type budget is not listed, because a proposal for it was derived.

QualityTarget

QualityTarget is what a rule observes.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
meta_guid string

The globally unique metadata GUID of the target table.

meta_type MetaType

path QualityTargetPath

Where the target lived when the rule was saved. It is display metadata, not identity: the GUID and its meta type are the identity.

columns string repeated

The columns the rule reads, as a snapshot for display. The column named in the config is authoritative; validation requires them to agree.

QualityTargetColumn

QualityTargetColumn is one column of a resolved target.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

type string

nullable bool

QualityTargetKey

QualityTargetKey names one target by the only pair that identifies it: the

metadata GUID and the object type. It is an address, not a snapshot — the

metadata browser sends the objects it is showing so one call returns their

trust signals.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
target_guid string

The target's metadata GUID. Required.

meta_type MetaType

The target's object type. Required, because a GUID alone does not identify a registry row across object types.

QualityTargetPath

QualityTargetPath is the display snapshot of where a target lived when the

rule was saved.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
instance string

database string

schema string

object string

column string

Display snapshot only. The checked column is the one named in the rule's typed config; this field may be empty for rules written before it was populated, and is empty for a table-level rule.

QualityTargetSchedule

QualityTargetSchedule is a target's one schedule: the cadence every enabled

check of the target runs at, and when the target next comes due. Scheduling is

per target, so all of its checks are planned and executed together. A target

runs either on a fixed interval or on a cron expression, never both.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
schedule_interval google.protobuf.Duration

How often the target's enabled checks run, between 15 minutes and 7 days. A cron target keeps the expression's nominal gap here as the cadence it falls back to when the expression is cleared, so the editor can seed interval mode from it; cron decides the actual occurrence.

next_run_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

When the scheduler next considers the target due. Unset while the target has no enabled check.

cron string

A standard five-field cron expression evaluated in timezone, for example "0 2 * * *" for every day at 02:00. Empty when the target runs on schedule_interval instead.

timezone string

The IANA time zone the cron expression is evaluated in, for example "Asia/Shanghai". Empty for an interval schedule. When a request leaves it empty, the server resolves it to the workspace's check time zone at save time and stores the resolved zone.

QualityTargetSummary

QualityTargetSummary is one row of the target directory: the target identity

plus the counts and health the row and the workspace header render.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
target QualityTarget

The target, named by GUID and object type. Its path is the snapshot stored with the rules; the column list is empty here.

rule_count int32

Live rules only; archived rules are excluded.

enabled_rule_count int32

paused_rule_count int32

column_count int32

Distinct columns the target's rules read.

open_issue_count int32

pending_draft_count int32

pending_label_count int32

worst_status QualityStatus

The worst latest result across the target's rules; UNSPECIFIED when no rule has run yet. ERROR outranks FAIL: a check that could not run needs attention more than one whose data failed.

last_run_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

schema_changed bool

Whether at least one rule was saved against a different target structure fingerprint than the registry currently records.

orphaned bool

Whether the target can no longer be resolved (the registry row, instance or database is gone). The rows stay readable because their target path is a snapshot, but runs are skipped.

latest_run QualityRun

The target's most recent run. A run belongs to one target, so it is the per-target batch summary the directory and the workspace show; unset when the target has never run.

run_count int32

How many dispatch batches belong to this target.

schedule QualityTargetSchedule

The target's schedule and next run. A target with rules always has a schedule; a target whose checks are all paused has an interval but no next run.

quality_score double optional

The target's quality score, 0-100, over its enabled rules' latest judged results. Unset when no enabled rule has been judged. The formula is the workspace's; see docs/data-quality.md.

scored_rule_count int32

recent_pass_rate double optional

The pass share of the target's most recent completed executions (at most 20): PASS / (PASS + WARN + FAIL). ERROR, SKIPPED and NOT_EVALUATED are excluded because they are not verdicts. Unset when none of them is judged; recent_execution_count is how many were.

recent_execution_count int32

covered_column_count int32

Column coverage: how many of the target's current registry columns at least one ENABLED check reads, and the target's current registry column count. A check that names no column, a paused check and a column that no longer exists in the registry cover nothing, so covered_column_count never exceeds total_column_count; both come from one registry read, which is what keeps that true while schema sync is rewriting the column list. A target whose registry row no longer resolves reports 0/0. The formula is the workspace coverage's; see docs/data-quality.md.

total_column_count int32

QualityThresholdSuggestion

QualityThresholdSuggestion is a threshold derived from the check's history. It

is a starting point for the editor, never a verdict: the values are rounded for

display, the method is stated, and nothing is written until the check is saved.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
thresholds QualityThresholds

The suggested bounds, in the trend's unit and shaped like the snapshot the check itself records: fail_value/warn_value for a single upper bound, and the fail/warn pairs for the two-sided row-count bounds. Unset when no suggestion could be derived; notice then says why.

sample_size int32

How many judged executions the suggestion was derived from.

method QualityThresholdSuggestionMethod

notice QualityTrendNotice

QualityThresholds

QualityThresholds is the threshold snapshot a result records, so a historical

result can be explained after the rule's thresholds changed. For

GREATER_THAN / LESS_THAN only value fields are set; for the range comparisons

the lower and upper bounds are.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
warn_value double optional

Unset means the rule has no warning level.

fail_value double optional

warn_value_upper double optional

fail_value_upper double optional

comparison QualityComparison

on_empty QualityEmptyBehavior

QualityTrendPoint

QualityTrendPoint is one day of result tallies.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
date string

The day, as YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.

pass int32

warn int32

fail int32

error int32

skipped int32

not_evaluated int32

total int32

RangeConfig

RangeConfig counts rows outside a bound pair. At least one bound is required;

the values are strings parsed with the column's type.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
column string

min string optional

max string optional

inclusive bool

Whether both bounds are inclusive. Default false, i.e. the interval is open on both ends.

fail_threshold double optional

warn_threshold double optional

RunQualityRulesRequest

FieldTypeLabelDescription
parent string

Format: workspaces/{workspace}. "workspaces/-" is the current workspace.

The rules to run, at most 200. At least one of rules, instance and target_guid must be set.

Restrict the selection to the enabled rules of one instance. Format: instances/{instance}

target_guid string

Restrict the selection to the enabled rules that watch this table.

RunQualityRulesResponse

FieldTypeLabelDescription
executions QualityExecution repeated

One execution per selected rule, planned and queued for the runner. All of them are PENDING when the response is returned; poll GetQualityExecution.

SchemaDriftColumn

SchemaDriftColumn is one column of the snapshot a schema-drift rule expects.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

type string

nullable bool optional

Whether the column is nullable. Unset means the rule does not judge nullability for this column: a snapshot written before nullability was compared stays usable and does not report a false drift. The editor and the API's fill-from-target path always set it.

SchemaDriftConfig

SchemaDriftConfig compares the live column list with the snapshot taken when

the rule was saved. The rule reads metadata only, so it costs the target

database nothing.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
expected_columns SchemaDriftColumn repeated

The snapshot. The API fills it from the current columns when a rule is created without one, and the editor lets a user adjust it.

check_types bool optional

Whether a changed column type or nullability is drift. Unset means true: either change is drift unless the rule author turns the check off.

check_order bool

Whether a changed column order is drift. Default false.

allow_extra_columns bool

Whether a column the snapshot does not name is drift. Default false.

fail_threshold double optional

Drift items tolerated. The metric is always COUNT here.

warn_threshold double optional

SegmentCheckConfig

SegmentCheckConfig fails when a segment that the check's recent executions

observed is missing from the current one. A segment is the distinct

combination of the grouping columns.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
columns string repeated

The columns that identify a segment (1-5).

baseline_runs int32

How many previous judged executions form the baseline. 0 means the default (3); the accepted range is 1-10. Executions judged against another target, or recorded before segment evidence existed, are skipped.

min_occurrences int32

How many of the baseline executions a segment must appear in to be expected in the current one. 0 means the default (2). It is clamped to the number of baseline runs actually available, so the second execution already judges.

fail_threshold double optional

warn_threshold double optional

SegmentObservation

SegmentObservation is the segment set one segment-check execution observed,

kept as the baseline the following executions are judged against.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
observed SegmentRecord repeated

The segments this execution saw, largest first. Bounded by a fixed cap, so a truncated observation carries only the largest segments.

new_segments SegmentRecord repeated

The observed segments the baseline did not have. They are evidence only: a new segment does not fail the check.

truncated bool

True when the observed set was cut off by the segment cap.

baseline_runs int32

How many previous executions formed the baseline; 0 means there was none.

expected_count int64

How many segments the baseline expected.

disappeared SegmentRecord repeated

The expected segments the current execution did not observe: the ones that failed the check. Each carries the last baseline run that saw it and its row count then. Empty when the check passed.

SegmentRecord

SegmentRecord is one segment: its key values and row count.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
values string repeated

One display-rendered value per grouping column, in the rule's column order.

row_count int64

last_seen google.protobuf.Timestamp

When the baseline last observed the segment. Unset for a segment this execution observed.

is_null bool repeated

Whether the matching value in values is SQL NULL. The list is parallel to values; a missing entry reads as not null.

masked bool repeated

Whether the matching value in values was redacted before storage. The list is parallel to values; a missing entry reads as not redacted.

value_digests string repeated

A digest of the full value behind each entry of values, hex encoded. Values are truncated for display; the digest is what tells two segments with the same 128-byte prefix apart across executions. The list is parallel to values; a missing entry reads as empty (fall back to the value).

SemanticLabelEvidence

SemanticLabelEvidence is why a label was assigned. It cites the inputs the

labeler saw so a reviewer can check the reasoning without re-running it.

FieldTypeLabelDescription

Columns whose values or context the label derives from.

metrics string repeated

Profile facts such as "null_rate=0.02" or "distinct=12".

lineage string repeated

Lineage relations that motivated the label, e.g. "join key of orders".

rationale string

SemanticLabelSuggestion

SemanticLabelSuggestion is a model-proposed semantic label for one column.

FieldTypeLabelDescription

label QualitySemanticType

confidence double

evidence SemanticLabelEvidence

suggested_rule_types QualityRuleType repeated

The rule types the deterministic mapping would suggest for this label, in display order. The model may rank types but may not invent one.

StandardCodeConfig

StandardCodeConfig validates one column against a national or industry

standard code. The standard fixes the value shape, the check digit where one

exists, and whether the value must exist in the standard's built-in code

table. The rule reads a bounded sample of the column and validates every row

in process, so its verdict is a sample verdict like cel_expression's.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
column string

standard QualityStandardCode

allow_null bool

When false (the default), a NULL value is a violation.

sample_rows int32

How many rows of the filtered relation one execution reads. 0 means the default (10000); the accepted range is 1-100000.

fail_threshold double optional

warn_threshold double optional

code_table string

Optional workspace code table the value must also exist in, as a "workspaces/{workspace}/qualityCodeTables/{quality_code_table}" resource name. Required for QUALITY_STANDARD_CODE_CUSTOM_CODE_TABLE; for a built-in standard it narrows the accepted values (for example a customer's current division list).

FieldTypeLabelDescription

FieldTypeLabelDescription
parent string

Format: workspaces/{workspace}. "workspaces/-" is the current workspace.

The target's metadata GUID. Required.

The target's object type. Optional when rules already exist, because their own target carries it.

How often the target's enabled checks run. Exactly one of schedule_interval and cron is set: a fixed interval between 15 minutes and 7 days, or a cron expression.

DataQualityService

DataQualityService manages the checks that watch the data itself: rules and

their executions.

A rule observes one target — a table, or one column of it — with a typed

check (row count, null percent, uniqueness, accepted values, ...). Scheduling

belongs to the target: every enabled check on a target runs together when the

target's schedule comes due, and a check can also run on demand. An execution

is one rule checked once: it is planned asynchronously, executed by the

runner, and polled until it reaches a state or an outcome. Batching rules for

scheduling is an internal concern and is not exposed as a resource.

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
ListQualityRules ListQualityRulesRequest ListQualityRulesResponse

List rules, newest first.
GetQualityRule GetQualityRuleRequest QualityRule

Read one rule, including its current revision and a summary of its most recent result.
CreateQualityRule CreateQualityRuleRequest QualityRule

Create a rule. The rule is validated and compiled before it is stored; a rejected rule is never persisted.
BatchCreateQualityRules BatchCreateQualityRulesRequest BatchCreateQualityRulesResponse

Create a batch of rules in one call, optionally from the suggestions they came from. Each item is validated and stored independently: a failure is reported in its own result and does not abort the other items.
BatchUpdateQualityRules BatchUpdateQualityRulesRequest BatchUpdateQualityRulesResponse

Update a batch of rules in one call. Each item is applied independently: a failure is reported in its own result and does not abort the other items. An item that names a stale revision fails on its own rather than overwriting a concurrent edit.
UpdateQualityRule UpdateQualityRuleRequest QualityRule

Update a rule. Every semantic edit appends a revision, so a historical result always stays explainable by the definition that produced it.
DeleteQualityRule DeleteQualityRuleRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete a rule. The rule, its revisions and results are only archived, never physically removed, so history stays readable.
ListQualityRuleTemplates ListQualityRuleTemplatesRequest ListQualityRuleTemplatesResponse

List the workspace's custom rule templates, newest first. Built-in templates are served by the client catalogue and are not part of this resource.
GetQualityRuleTemplate GetQualityRuleTemplateRequest QualityRuleTemplate

Read one custom rule template.
CreateQualityRuleTemplate CreateQualityRuleTemplateRequest QualityRuleTemplate

Create a custom rule template. A template is a check type and its parameters: target-bound fields (columns, filter) are cleared by the server before it is stored.
UpdateQualityRuleTemplate UpdateQualityRuleTemplateRequest QualityRuleTemplate

Update a custom rule template's title, description, severity, dimension or parameters. The same target-bound fields are cleared.
DeleteQualityRuleTemplate DeleteQualityRuleTemplateRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete a custom rule template. Checks already created from it are unaffected.
ListQualityCodeTables ListQualityCodeTablesRequest ListQualityCodeTablesResponse

List the workspace's code tables. A list response carries each table's value count but not its values; read one table with GetQualityCodeTable.
GetQualityCodeTable GetQualityCodeTableRequest QualityCodeTable

Read one code table including its values.
CreateQualityCodeTable CreateQualityCodeTableRequest QualityCodeTable

Create a workspace code table. Values are sorted, de-duplicated and capped by the server, so an import is idempotent.
UpdateQualityCodeTable UpdateQualityCodeTableRequest QualityCodeTable

Update a code table's title, description or values. Replacing the values is the import path.
DeleteQualityCodeTable DeleteQualityCodeTableRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete a code table. A table still referenced by a rule or a template is refused with FailedPrecondition rather than silently breaking those checks.
PreviewQualityRule PreviewQualityRuleRequest PreviewQualityRuleResponse

Validate and compile a rule without saving it: config validation, filter validation and a `LIMIT 0` probe against the target's read-only data source. It writes nothing and creates no run.
RunQualityRules RunQualityRulesRequest RunQualityRulesResponse

Execute rules now. One execution is planned per selected rule; the call returns them all as PENDING after queueing them. Clients poll GetQualityExecution for each execution's state and outcome.
ListQualityExecutions ListQualityExecutionsRequest ListQualityExecutionsResponse

List executions, newest first.
GetQualityExecution GetQualityExecutionRequest QualityExecution

Read one execution: its state, verdict, and the evidence behind it.
GetQualityRuleTrend GetQualityRuleTrendRequest QualityRuleTrend

Read one check's judged values over its recent executions, the band its current thresholds draw, and a threshold suggestion derived from that history. It is a read model over the stored executions: nothing is written, audited or measured against the target database. Only executions that reached a judged verdict (PASS, WARN or FAIL) carry a value, so only those appear as points; a check that has never been judged has no trend rather than a fabricated flat line.
ExportQualityExecutions ExportQualityExecutionsRequest ExportQualityDataChunk stream

Export the executions the same filters select as ListQualityExecutions as one CSV document, streamed in slices. This is a file download, not a list: it stops at max_rows and reports the running row count on every slice. Rows are read page by page, so the file is not a consistent snapshot: a row written while the export runs may fall in this file or the next. A stream error means the file is incomplete and must be discarded — only a completed stream is a document. No (google.api.http) annotation: this is a server-streaming method, and the REST gateway cannot carry one. The browser reaches the Connect endpoint directly, the way it does for ExplainSQL.
ListQualityRuns ListQualityRunsRequest ListQualityRunsResponse

List runs, newest first. A run is one dispatch batch that belongs to one target: the executions one scheduler tick or one manual request planned for that target. Runs are the batch-level read model the execution directory groups by target; the run itself carries the target and its counts.
GetQualityRun GetQualityRunRequest QualityRun

Read one run: its target, state, verdict and counts.
ListQualityIssues ListQualityIssuesRequest ListQualityIssuesResponse

List quality issues, newest first.
GetQualityIssue GetQualityIssueRequest QualityIssue

Read one quality issue.

This is a file download, not a list: it stops at max_rows and reports the running row count on every slice. Rows are read page by page, so the file is not a consistent snapshot: a row written while the export runs may fall in this file or the next. A stream error means the file is incomplete and must be discarded — only a completed stream is a document. No (google.api.http) annotation, for the same reason as ExportQualityExecutions.
UpdateQualityIssue UpdateQualityIssueRequest QualityIssue

Acknowledge, resolve or mute one quality issue.
ListQualitySuggestions ListQualitySuggestionsRequest ListQualitySuggestionsResponse

List the review queue of model-proposed rule drafts and semantic labels, newest first.

Read one queued suggestion. The queue is paged with ListQualitySuggestions; this exists so a deep link can open one draft without reading the pages.
UpdateQualitySuggestion UpdateQualitySuggestionRequest QualitySuggestion

BatchUpdateQualitySuggestions BatchUpdateQualitySuggestionsRequest BatchUpdateQualitySuggestionsResponse

Accept or reject many queued suggestions in one call. Each decision is independent: a failure is reported in its own result and does not abort the rest.
CreateQualitySuggestionJob CreateQualitySuggestionJobRequest QualitySuggestionJob

Start a background AI drafting job over one or more tables. The call returns as soon as the job is queued: the runner asks the model for each target in turn, and clients poll GetQualitySuggestionJob (or list the jobs) for progress. Queued suggestions appear in the review queue like any other.
GetQualitySuggestionJob GetQualitySuggestionJobRequest QualitySuggestionJob

Ask a drafting job to stop. A pending job is canceled immediately; a running job finishes its current target, marks the rest skipped and ends CANCELED. Suggestions already queued are kept.

Read the raw request and response bodies of one failed target when runtime debug mode captured them. The target's diagnostic carries the correlation id and says whether a body is available; llm_debug_log keeps it for seven days.

RecommendQualityChecks RecommendQualityChecksRequest RecommendQualityChecksResponse

Recommend checks for one table from its stored column profiles. The pass is deterministic: it needs no model, no provider configuration and no connection to the target database. Like every other generation pass it queues PENDING rule drafts only; a reviewer still decides which drafts become checks. The request refuses columns without a fresh profile, pointing at ProfileColumns.
ExplainQualityExecution ExplainQualityExecutionRequest ExplainQualityExecutionResponse stream

Explain one failed execution as a stream of hypotheses. No (google.api.http) annotation: this is a server-streaming method, and the REST gateway cannot carry one. The browser reaches the Connect endpoint directly, the way it does for ExplainSQL.
GetQualityOverview GetQualityOverviewRequest QualityOverview

Read the workspace's quality summary: how many rules and issues exist, how the last day went, and the per-day tallies the overview chart draws.
GetQualityConsumptionCoverage GetQualityConsumptionCoverageRequest GetQualityConsumptionCoverageResponse

Read how much of the data other assets consume is watched. Unlike the overview's coverage, whose denominator is every monitorable registry object, this answers a consumption question: of the assets whose lineage shows another object reading them, how many have an enabled check? The two ratios have different denominators and are deliberately not combined. It is a separate read because answering it costs one grouped scan of the lineage table, which the overview must not pay on every load.
ListQualityTargets ListQualityTargetsRequest ListQualityTargetsResponse

List the targets (tables or views) that have quality rules, one row per target. The counts, the worst latest result and the pending draft tally are aggregated by the database, so the directory does not page through every rule to answer "which table needs attention?".

Export the targets the same filters select as ListQualityTargets as one CSV document, streamed in slices. This is a file download, not a list: it stops at max_rows and reports the running row count on every slice. Rows are read page by page, so the file is not a consistent snapshot: a row written while the export runs may fall in this file or the next. A stream error means the file is incomplete and must be discarded — only a completed stream is a document. No (google.api.http) annotation, for the same reason as ExportQualityExecutions.
GetQualityTarget GetQualityTargetRequest GetQualityTargetResponse

Read one target's workspace: its rules (with their latest results), the unresolved issues and the target's columns, in one call. AI drafts are not part of the response (reading them needs the suggest permission). The target is named by GUID because a target is not a resource of its own.
GetQualityTargetImpact GetQualityTargetImpactRequest GetQualityTargetImpactResponse

Explain a target's quality state by its lineage: the assets its data reaches downstream, and the upstream targets whose checks failed or whose structure changed in the window before a reference instant. Both lists are bounded walks over the recorded lineage, so a target with no recorded edges has no impact to report — which is not the same as having no consumers.
AcknowledgeQualityTargetSchema AcknowledgeQualityTargetSchemaRequest AcknowledgeQualityTargetSchemaResponse

Acknowledge that a target's structure changed and re-baseline its checks. Every non-archived check whose saved structure snapshot differs from the target's current fingerprint gets the current fingerprint, which clears the schema-changed signal. The checks themselves are untouched: re-baselining is a fact about which shape the checks were reviewed against, not a change to their definition, so it does not write a rule revision. Idempotent: a second call with nothing to do returns zero.
ExportQualityReport ExportQualityReportRequest ExportQualityReportResponse

Render one target's quality report as a self-contained HTML document: the current state, the recent trend, the checks, the unresolved problems, a capped sample summary and the monitoring basis. The document carries its own styles and chart and loads nothing external, so it can be forwarded as a file. The export is audited because it is a bulk read of quality evidence. The report includes real sample values from failed checks (capped), so it is a wider disclosure than the rules.list permission usually implies; the document itself warns about forwarding it. Its HTML body never enters the audit ledger (see ExportQualityReportResponse.html_content).
UpdateQualityTargetSchedule UpdateQualityTargetScheduleRequest QualityTargetSchedule

Update one target's schedule: how often its enabled checks run. Scheduling is per target, so this replaces the per-check schedule; a change takes effect from the next slot and never runs the target immediately.
GetQualityTargetSchedule GetQualityTargetScheduleRequest QualityTargetSchedule

Read one target's schedule without the target's rules, results and issues. A rule lifecycle change can move the target's next run; the workspace re-reads just this instead of the whole target after every check edit.
GetQualityContract GetQualityContractRequest QualityContract

Read one target's contract: its target-level defaults, the published version, and whether the live rules differ from that snapshot.
ListQualityPlans ListQualityPlansRequest ListQualityPlansResponse

ListQualityPlans lists the read-only monitoring plan projection for every target with live rules. It is the directory the plan write path will grow from; it does not write anything.
ListQualityCoverageGaps ListQualityCoverageGapsRequest ListQualityCoverageGapsResponse

ListQualityCoverageGaps flattens the plan projection to the unsatisfied declared coverage: one row per target property that a live rule does not implement. Read-only, like ListQualityPlans.
UpdateQualityContract UpdateQualityContractRequest QualityContract

Update the target-level defaults. The filter is ANDed into every rule on the target at compile time; the default severity only seeds newly authored rules and never rewrites an existing rule. The target's schedule is updated through UpdateQualityTargetSchedule.
PublishQualityContract PublishQualityContractRequest PublishQualityContractResponse

Publish the live rules and settings as the target's next contract version. Republishing an unchanged contract is a no-op that returns the existing version (no_changes=true).
CreateQualityInvestigation CreateQualityInvestigationRequest QualityInvestigation

Record one investigation: an agent's hypotheses, deterministic evidence references, verdict and cost on one event. It never changes the check's verdict or an issue's state. The agent needs autonomy enabled.
GetQualityInvestigation GetQualityInvestigationRequest QualityInvestigation

Read one investigation.
ListQualityInvestigations ListQualityInvestigationsRequest ListQualityInvestigationsResponse

List investigations, newest first.
GetQualityActionPolicy GetQualityActionPolicyRequest QualityActionPolicy

Read the WS2 action catalog and how the autonomy policy would decide each action for an agent right now. Read-only: it exposes the policy, it does not change it.
CreateQualityMemory CreateQualityMemoryRequest QualityMemory

Record one memory: an asset fact, a decision with its structured reason, or an event. An agent may write asset facts directly; a decision or an event it writes stays PROPOSED until a person confirms it.
ListQualityMemories ListQualityMemoriesRequest ListQualityMemoriesResponse

List memories. Expired confirmations read as EXPIRED; superseded ones stay visible for the correction path.
ConfirmQualityMemory ConfirmQualityMemoryRequest QualityMemory

Confirm or reject a PROPOSED memory. A person's judgment is what turns it into knowledge; nothing else confirms it.
DeleteQualityMemory DeleteQualityMemoryRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete a memory. Administrator cleanup; the row is kept out of reads, and the audit row records who removed it.
StageQualityPlan StageQualityPlanRequest QualityContract

Write the target's plan declaration without touching its settings. This is the one write an agent principal may make; an agent call is refused while the workspace kill switch or the agent itself is disabled.
CreateQualityChangeRequest CreateQualityChangeRequestRequest QualityChangeRequest

Create a batch of typed changes against one target. It stays PROPOSED until a person decides; creating it changes nothing on the target. An agent principal may only create PROPOSED requests, and only while autonomy is enabled.
GetQualityChangeRequest GetQualityChangeRequestRequest QualityChangeRequest

Read one change request, with its items and per-item results.
ListQualityChangeRequests ListQualityChangeRequestsRequest ListQualityChangeRequestsResponse

List change requests, newest first.
CreateQualityAgent CreateQualityAgentRequest CreateQualityAgentResponse

Create an agent principal and return its bearer token once. The agent is an independent principal whose only workspace role is the quality agent role; its token is a normal access token for that principal, so disabling the agent makes every token it issued unusable. Administrator only.
ListQualityAgents ListQualityAgentsRequest ListQualityAgentsResponse

List the workspace's agent principals, without tokens.
DisableQualityAgent DisableQualityAgentRequest QualityAgent

Disable an agent principal. Its tokens stop authenticating immediately; the agent row stays for the audit trail.
RotateQualityAgentToken RotateQualityAgentTokenRequest RotateQualityAgentTokenResponse

Rotate an agent's bearer token: mint a new one and invalidate every token minted before this call. The token is returned once.
DecideQualityChangeRequest DecideQualityChangeRequestRequest QualityChangeRequest

Approve or reject a change request. Approving applies each item through its existing path and returns a result per item; rejecting records the structured reasons. A stale base version expires the request instead of rebasing it.
ListQualityContractRevisions ListQualityContractRevisionsRequest ListQualityContractRevisionsResponse

List the target's published contract versions, newest first.
GetQualityContractRevision GetQualityContractRevisionRequest GetQualityContractRevisionResponse

Read one published contract version with its ordered checks, so a client can show a diff without downloading every version.
GetQualityLLMUsage GetQualityLLMUsageRequest QualityLLMUsage

Read today's data quality LLM usage and the effective limits (the workspace settings, with server defaults resolved). The counters are process state: a restart resets them and they roll over at 00:00 UTC.

EnvironmentService

EnvironmentService manages the workspace's environments. An environment is a

small, workspace-scoped resource ("environments/{id}") that instances are

tagged with; databases inherit their instance's environment.

Environments are stored in the ENVIRONMENT workspace setting, not in a table

of their own. The id is derived from the title on create and is immutable:

instances store the raw id, so renaming only changes the display title.

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription

List the workspace environments. Readable by every workspace member: the instance forms and the metadata filters need the list, and those pages are open to every member.

Create an environment.
UpdateEnvironment UpdateEnvironmentRequest Environment

Update an environment. Only title, color and tags are mutable; the resource name (the id) is not.
DeleteEnvironment DeleteEnvironmentRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete an environment. An environment still assigned to a live instance cannot be deleted.

Binding

Binding binds one role to a set of principals. It is the v1 view of the

stored IAM binding; the workspace IAM policy is written whole through

IamService.SetWorkspaceIamPolicy.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
role string

The role that is assigned to the members. Format: roles/{role}

members string repeated

The principals requesting access. For users: users/{userUID}; for groups: groups/{email}; the pseudo-member allUsers matches every authenticated principal, including the ones who register later, so it is accepted only on the roles/workspaceMember baseline binding. That binding is server-managed: it cannot be edited or dropped, and a Set whose policy omits it is rejected.

condition google.type.Expr

The condition that is associated with this binding. When present the binding applies only while the condition evaluates to true.

IamPolicyView

IamPolicyView is an IAM policy together with its etag. The etag is returned

by Get and must be supplied on Set for optimistic concurrency: a Set whose

etag does not match the stored policy's etag is rejected with

connect.CodeAborted so the caller can re-fetch and retry. An empty etag

skips the check (first write).

by metaxisdata.iam.getPolicy / metaxisdata.iam.setPolicy.

OAuth2IdentityProviderConfig is an OAuth2 provider's configuration.

The authorization endpoint the browser is sent to. Not used by the server: the client builds the authorize URL from it.

The token endpoint. Required.

The client secret. Required on create. Never returned by a read, and an empty value on update keeps the stored one. It is stored encrypted with the deployment's data key (see `backend/common/crypto`), so a database reader without the key cannot authenticate as this application to the provider.

The claim mapping.

Whether to skip TLS certificate verification on the provider's endpoints. Off by default and off is the only safe setting: with it on, anyone able to intercept the connection can forge the userinfo response and take over every account bound to this provider. IdentityProviderType

NameNumberDescription

OAUTH2 1

OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow.

OAuth2AuthStyle

NameNumberDescription
OAUTH2_AUTH_STYLE_UNSPECIFIED 0

IN_PARAMS 1

IN_PARAMS sends the "client_id" and "client_secret" in the POST body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded parameters.
IN_HEADER 2

IN_HEADER sends the client_id and client_secret using HTTP Basic Authorization, as described in the OAuth2 RFC 6749 section 2.3.1.

IdentityProviderService

IdentityProviderService is the admin surface for SSO.

It is the write path for the `idp` table: before it existed the only way to

configure a provider was to insert SQL by hand, so the login page had nothing

to point at and `client_secret` could not be encrypted on write.

ListIdentityProviders is deliberately readable without credentials: the login

page renders one button per configured provider before the visitor has a

session. It never returns a secret, so a provider's non-secret half (auth URL,

client id, scopes, mapping) is what an anonymous caller can see.

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
GetIdentityProvider GetIdentityProviderRequest IdentityProvider

Get an identity provider, including the non-secret half of its config.
ListIdentityProviders ListIdentityProvidersRequest ListIdentityProvidersResponse

List every configured identity provider. Public so the login page can render the enabled SSO targets without credentials. The `permission` annotation is kept beside `allow_without_credential`, as on `SettingService.GetWorkspaceProfileSetting`: the latter wins in the interceptor, and the annotation is what records the permission this read belongs to in the catalog.
CreateIdentityProvider CreateIdentityProviderRequest IdentityProvider

Create an identity provider. The id becomes the final segment of the resource name and is immutable, so it is derived from the title by the client and checked here.
UpdateIdentityProvider UpdateIdentityProviderRequest IdentityProvider

Update an identity provider. Only title, domain and config are mutable; the resource name is not. An empty secret in the config means "keep the stored one", because the read path never hands the stored secret back.
DeleteIdentityProvider DeleteIdentityProviderRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete an identity provider. Accounts bound to it keep their binding rows but can no longer sign in through it: the binding records the subject the provider assigned, which no longer resolves to a configured provider. Re-creating the provider with the same id makes those accounts reachable again, which is why the id matters.
TestIdentityProvider TestIdentityProviderRequest TestIdentityProviderResponse

TestIdentityProvider completes a real authorization-code exchange against a stored provider and reports the identity it resolves. The provider has to be saved first: the exchange needs the stored client secret, and the browser is never given it. The caller obtains an authorization code by sending an administrator's browser to the provider's authorization endpoint with `{external_url}/oauth/callback` as the redirect URI — the same URI a login uses — so no extra callback has to be registered with the provider. The client marks that state record as a test so the callback page tests instead of signing the administrator in. This verifies the client id and secret end to end, which endpoint reachability alone cannot.
ListIdentityProviderBindings ListIdentityProviderBindingsRequest ListIdentityProviderBindingsResponse

List the accounts bound to an identity provider subject. A binding is what a login resolves against, so this is the read an administrator needs before moving or deleting an account: without it the only way to see why a login lands on an account is SQL.
DeleteIdentityProviderBinding DeleteIdentityProviderBindingRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

DeleteIdentityProviderBinding unbinds one account from one provider subject. The account loses that way in but keeps every other one; nothing else about it changes. Deleting the last binding of an account whose password was replaced on adoption leaves it reachable only by an administrator resetting the password, so the caller is expected to confirm before doing it. It is gated by `update`, not `delete`, and the settings page hides the button behind the same permission: this edits a provider's configuration, and `delete` is reserved for removing a provider outright.
