AnalysisScope

AnalysisScope is one resolution context for a SQL statement: a named database

(MySQL family) or schema (PostgreSQL-like). `name` is an opaque

caller-supplied label that is echoed back so results can be attributed; the

server attaches no meaning to it.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

guid string

The metadata GUID of the database or schema the statement is resolved against, e.g. "instance_1;db2" or "instance_1;db2;public". It only supplies the default instance/database/schema for unqualified names; the existence of the database or schema is not validated.

AnalyzeSQLDiagnostic

AnalyzeSQLDiagnostic is one thing an analysis could not represent.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
category DiagnosticCategory

subject string

What the diagnostic is about, the way the analyzer names it: the statement or clause shape it does not model ("MERGE", "WITH before INSERT"), or the clause a reference was written in ("a CTE body").

reference string

The identifier a reference diagnostic could not resolve, written the way the SQL writes it ("t.c", "t", "c"). Empty when the diagnostic is about a shape.

detail string

The cause, for a diagnostic that needs one: the parser defect behind a skipped clause, or the catalog error behind a degraded lookup.

AnalyzeSQLRelation

FieldTypeLabelDescription
source_guid string

The table-level GUID of the source column, with instance/database/schema filled in from the scope. It is reported even when the object is not in the metadata registry.

source_column string

source_type MetaType

TABLE/VIEW/... when the object is found in the metadata registry.

target_guid string

Empty when the target is a synthetic object that only exists inside the statement (the result of a bare SELECT, a CTE, a subquery). In that case target_column is the output alias of the query and is_temp is true.

target_column string

target_type MetaType

relation_type RelationType

transformations Transformation repeated

is_temp bool

AnalyzeSQLRequest

FieldTypeLabelDescription
scopes AnalysisScope repeated

The scopes to resolve the statement against, at most 10. The statement is analyzed once per scope, independently: the scopes may live on different instances and even different engines, and their results are not merged. Selecting several scopes does not discover cross-scope relations that are absent from the metadata.

sql_text string

The SQL statement to analyze.

AnalyzeSQLResponse

FieldTypeLabelDescription
results AnalyzeSQLResult repeated

One result per requested scope, in the same order.

warnings string repeated

Warnings that apply to the request as a whole.

AnalyzeSQLResult

FieldTypeLabelDescription
scope_name string

The scope name from the request, echoed back.

scope_guid string

relations AnalyzeSQLRelation repeated

warnings string repeated

Warnings that only affect this scope, such as an engine without a lineage analyzer. They never fail the whole request.

diagnostics AnalyzeSQLDiagnostic repeated

What the analysis could not represent. relations is everything it did resolve; a diagnostic says why an edge may be missing, which the relations alone cannot say. An analyzer that cannot parse the statement is not reported here: that fails the scope instead.

omitted_diagnostic_count int32

How many diagnostics the server's per-analysis bound left out, so a caller can tell a complete list from a truncated one.

LineageCount

LineageCount is one object's degree in the stored graph, at table level: how

many distinct objects its column-level relations connect it to. The count is

of objects, not of relations, so two tables joined on five columns are one

upstream object rather than five.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
guid string

upstream_count int32

downstream_count int32

LineageNode

LineageNode is one object in the multi-level graph. Only column-level edges

are stored, so the table-level relations are the collapse of those edges: an

object whose definition yields no column-level relation at all (for example a

bare `SELECT count(*)`, or an object that was never synced) does not appear.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
guid string

meta_type MetaType

name string

The object name; the dataset name for an external dataset.

database string

schema string

instance_id string

distance int32

Hops from the root: negative upstream, positive downstream.

LineageRelation

FieldTypeLabelDescription
id int64

meta_guid string

meta_type MetaType

source_guid string

source_column string

source_type MetaType

target_guid string

target_column string

target_type MetaType

relation_type RelationType

transformations Transformation repeated

updated_at google.protobuf.Timestamp

Transformation

Transformation describes one step of how a source column becomes a target

column, derived from the view's SQL.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
operation string

The transformation kind: DELETE, UNION, PROJECT, FUNCTION, AGGREGATE, WINDOW, OPERATOR or CASE.

expression string

The text representation of the expression (most kinds).

function_name string

The function name (FUNCTION, AGGREGATE, WINDOW).

arguments string repeated

The function arguments (FUNCTION).

group_keys string repeated

The GROUP BY keys (AGGREGATE).

partition_by string repeated

The PARTITION BY columns (WINDOW).

order_by string repeated

The ORDER BY columns (WINDOW).

op_type string

The operator type, e.g. "+", "=" (OPERATOR).

condition string

The WHERE condition (DELETE).

all bool

Whether a set operation keeps duplicate rows: true for UNION ALL, INTERSECT ALL and EXCEPT ALL, false for their plain forms (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT).

DiagnosticCategory

DiagnosticCategory classifies what an analysis could not represent. The

categories call for different action: a shape the analyzer does not model is a

coverage gap in the analyzer, while a reference that does not resolve is

usually the SQL naming something the analyzer cannot see.

NameNumberDescription
DIAGNOSTIC_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED 0

DIAGNOSTIC_CATEGORY_NOT_MODELLED 1

A statement or clause shape the analyzer does not model yet.
DIAGNOSTIC_CATEGORY_UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE 2

A reference that resolved to nothing.
DIAGNOSTIC_CATEGORY_AMBIGUOUS_REFERENCE 3

A reference a single-valued position could not choose between, which is an unqualified name several relations in scope own.
DIAGNOSTIC_CATEGORY_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE 4

A metadata lookup that failed. The analysis carried on with the relation's columns unknown, so its edges are degraded rather than complete.

LineageType

NameNumberDescription
LINEAGE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED 0

SOURCE 1

TARGET 2

RelationType

NameNumberDescription
RELATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED 0

DIRECT 1

DIRECT means the source column is directly used in the target column without transformation. For example: select source_column as target_column from table.
INDIRECT 2

INDIRECT means the source column is used in the target column with transformation. For example: select concat(source_column, 'abc') as target_column
JOIN 3

JOIN means the source column is a join key: it decides which rows the target receives without its value reaching the target column. The target column is empty, because the influence is on the rows rather than on one column.
GROUP 4

GROUP means the source column was aggregated into the target column. For example: select count(source_column) as target_column from table
UNION 5

UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT mean the source column is one arm of the set operation that produced the target column.
INTERSECT 6

EXCEPT 7

UNKNOWN 8

UNKNOWN is carried so a stored relation of an unrecognized kind round-trips. No analyzer produces it.

LineageService

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
GetLineage GetLineageRequest GetLineageResponse

GetLineage returns the lineage relations for the given metadata. The lineage relations can be either source lineage or target lineage, depending on the lineage_type specified in the request. If lineage_type is not specified, both source and target lineage will be returned.
GetLineageCounts GetLineageCountsRequest GetLineageCountsResponse

GetLineageCounts returns how many distinct objects each requested object has upstream and downstream. A node's degree cannot be read off its neighbours' relations, so a graph that labels every node it draws would otherwise cost one GetLineage per node; this answers a whole set from two aggregates. Only the counts are returned, never the relations themselves.
GetLineageForContext GetLineageForContextRequest GetLineageForContextResponse

GetLineageForContext retrieves the field-level lineage graph derived from a specific SQL context (e.g., view, stored procedure).
AnalyzeSQL AnalyzeSQLRequest AnalyzeSQLResponse

AnalyzeSQL parses an arbitrary SQL statement and returns its column-level relations, resolved against one or more analysis scopes. The analysis is stateless: nothing is persisted and no lineage runner is triggered, so the result describes this statement only and is not part of the stored graph.
GetLineageGraph GetLineageGraphRequest GetLineageGraphResponse

GetLineageGraph returns the multi-level lineage graph around one metadata object in a single call, instead of expanding it one hop at a time with GetLineage.

Methods with HTTP bindings

Method Name Method Pattern Body
GetLineage GET /v1/lineages
GetLineageCounts POST /v1/lineages:counts *
GetLineageForContext GET /v1/lineages:context
AnalyzeSQL POST /v1/lineages:analyzeSql *
GetLineageGraph GET /v1/lineages:graph

The answer budget one analysis requests from this profile, in output tokens. Zero means the server default (32768); an explicit value must be 256-131072. The provider or model may cap lower: the first request that exceeds it is retried once at 4096 tokens, and a still-rejected request is reported on the failed analysis as PROVIDER_STATUS. An update with an empty field mask writes this field only when it is non-zero (proto3 cannot distinguish an omitted int32 from an explicit zero); send an explicit `max_output_tokens` mask to reset it to the server default.

DataQualityNotificationKind

DataQualityNotificationKind is the event a data quality notification reports.

NameNumberDescription
DATA_QUALITY_NOTIFICATION_KIND_UNSPECIFIED 0

DATA_QUALITY_NOTIFICATION_KIND_ISSUE_OPENED 1

A rule started failing: an issue was opened.
DATA_QUALITY_NOTIFICATION_KIND_ISSUE_RECOVERED 2

A previously failing rule passes again: its issue resolved itself.
DATA_QUALITY_NOTIFICATION_KIND_EXECUTION_FAILED 3

A rule could not be executed at all. This is not a data failure.
DATA_QUALITY_NOTIFICATION_KIND_STORM_SUMMARY 4

One run failed so many rules that the individual messages were merged.
DATA_QUALITY_NOTIFICATION_KIND_TARGET_SCHEMA_CHANGED 5

A monitored target's structure changed since its checks were saved. It is a registry fact, not a data failure: the checks were written against a shape that has moved, so they are worth reviewing. The detail names the target and no rule, because one change is one event for every check on the target.

decides the config shape and which credential fields are required.

NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_KIND_UNSPECIFIED 0

NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_KIND_WEBHOOK 1

A generic HTTP endpoint that receives the delivery JSON, optionally signed.
NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_KIND_DINGTALK 2

A DingTalk group robot, optionally signed.
NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_KIND_WECOM 3

A WeCom group robot. Its bot key is part of the endpoint.
NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_KIND_FEISHU 4

A Feishu custom bot, optionally signed.
NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_KIND_EMAIL 5

An email sent through the workspace email setting.

NotificationDeliveryState

NotificationDeliveryState is the lifecycle of one outbound delivery.

NameNumberDescription
NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0

NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_STATE_PENDING 1

Waiting for its next attempt, or for a retry an administrator asked for.
NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_STATE_SENDING 2

Leased by a dispatcher.
NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_STATE_SENT 3

Delivered. Terminal.
NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_STATE_DEAD 4

Out of automatic attempts; an administrator can retry it.

NotificationSeverity

NotificationSeverity ranks a notification for its recipient.

NameNumberDescription
NOTIFICATION_SEVERITY_UNSPECIFIED 0

NOTIFICATION_SEVERITY_INFO 1

NOTIFICATION_SEVERITY_WARNING 2

NOTIFICATION_SEVERITY_ERROR 3

NotificationType

NotificationType is what a notification is about. It selects which detail

message the notification carries.

NameNumberDescription
NOTIFICATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED 0

NOTIFICATION_TYPE_SCHEMA_SYNC 1

The outcome of one schema sync operation.
NOTIFICATION_TYPE_OPENLINEAGE 2

An OpenLineage ingestion failure, or a dataset that could not be matched to a registered instance.
NOTIFICATION_TYPE_DATA_QUALITY 3

A data quality rule opened, recovered, failed to execute, or failed in a storm that was merged into one summary.
NOTIFICATION_TYPE_DATA_QUALITY_DIGEST 4

The workspace's scheduled data quality digest: one summary of the period's executions, problems and owners. It has no in-app copy; only the outbound channels subscribed to this type receive it.

OpenLineageFailureKind

OpenLineageFailureKind is why an OpenLineage request produced no lineage.

NameNumberDescription
OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_UNSPECIFIED 0

OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_INVALID_EVENT 1

The event could not be parsed, or crossed a per-event limit.
OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_LIMIT_EXCEEDED 2

The request body or the batch crossed a transport limit.
OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_SCOPE_MISMATCH 3

The event's namespace is not the one the ingestion key is scoped to.
OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_PERSIST_FAILED 4

The event could not be persisted.
OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_PROCESS_FAILED 5

The event was persisted but its lineage could not be derived.
OPENLINEAGE_FAILURE_KIND_NAMESPACE_UNMAPPED 6

The dataset matched no registered instance and was stored as an external dataset, so any lineage naming it points at something the registry does not describe. Check the instance's data source host and port, or add a namespace mapping.

SyncDatabaseState

SyncDatabaseState is one database's outcome within a sync operation.

NameNumberDescription
SYNC_DATABASE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0

SYNC_DATABASE_STATE_SUCCEEDED 1

SYNC_DATABASE_STATE_FAILED 2

SYNC_DATABASE_STATE_UNFINISHED 3

The operation ended before this database produced a result, because its deadline passed or its instance disappeared.

SyncTrigger

SyncTrigger is what started the sync operation a notification reports.

NameNumberDescription
SYNC_TRIGGER_UNSPECIFIED 0

SYNC_TRIGGER_MANUAL 1

A user asked for it. The initiator is the recipient.
SYNC_TRIGGER_BACKGROUND 2

The periodic scan asked for it, so there is no initiator and the workspace administrators are the recipients.

NotificationService

NotificationService serves the caller's own in-app messages — the outcome of

a sync operation they asked for, and the ingestion failures a workspace

administrator needs to see — and the workspace's outbound delivery channels,

which administrators configure.

The inbox methods carry no (metaxisdata.v1.permission) annotation and none is

reachable without credentials: an inbox belongs to one principal, which the

workspace-scoped IAM catalog cannot express, so every handler scopes its query

by the authenticated caller's id, the same way UserService's self-service

paths do. The outbound methods are workspace configuration and carry the

settings permissions: reads use settings.get, writes, the test send and the

delivery retry use settings.update.

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
ListNotifications ListNotificationsRequest ListNotificationsResponse

List the caller's notifications, newest first.
GetUnreadNotificationCount GetUnreadNotificationCountRequest GetUnreadNotificationCountResponse

Count the caller's unread notifications, and the subset of them written since the caller last opened the inbox.
MarkNotificationsSeen MarkNotificationsSeenRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Record that the caller has opened the inbox, which clears the badge. No notification is marked read: a message stays unread until it is clicked or the caller marks everything read.
BatchMarkNotificationsRead BatchMarkNotificationsReadRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Mark the named notifications read. Already-read notifications are left alone, so the call is idempotent.
MarkAllNotificationsRead MarkAllNotificationsReadRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Mark every unread notification of the caller read.
DeleteNotification DeleteNotificationRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete one of the caller's notifications.
SubscribeNotifications SubscribeNotificationsRequest SubscribeNotificationsResponse stream

Stream the caller's notifications as they are written, until the connection ends or the server ends it. No (google.api.http) annotation: this is a server-streaming method, and the REST gateway cannot carry one — it answers "streaming calls are not yet supported in the in-process transport", as the generated ExplainSQL gateway route does. The browser reaches the Connect endpoint directly, the way it does for ExplainSQL.
ListNotificationChannels ListNotificationChannelsRequest ListNotificationChannelsResponse

List the outbound channels administrators have configured. The list is not paginated: a workspace configures a handful of destinations, and the delivery path reads the whole set anyway.
GetNotificationChannel GetNotificationChannelRequest NotificationChannel

Read one outbound channel. The credential is never returned.
CreateNotificationChannel CreateNotificationChannelRequest NotificationChannel

Create one outbound channel. The secret is write-only: it is encrypted before it is stored and is never returned.
UpdateNotificationChannel UpdateNotificationChannelRequest NotificationChannel

Update one outbound channel. An omitted secret keeps the stored one; a present secret replaces it.
DeleteNotificationChannel DeleteNotificationChannelRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete one outbound channel and the deliveries still queued for it.
TestNotificationChannel TestNotificationChannelRequest TestNotificationChannelResponse

Post a test message through one stored channel and report what the endpoint answered. An email channel sends the message through the workspace SMTP setting instead, and its answer is empty. It queues no delivery and is not audited: it is a diagnostic probe that changes nothing, and the endpoint's answer is third-party text that does not belong in the permanent ledger.
ListNotificationDeliveries ListNotificationDeliveriesRequest ListNotificationDeliveriesResponse

List outbound deliveries, newest first, for administrators to diagnose a channel.
RetryNotificationDelivery RetryNotificationDeliveryRequest NotificationDelivery

Requeue one delivery: a DEAD delivery becomes PENDING again and a delivered or waiting one is left as it is.
ListNotificationRoutes ListNotificationRoutesRequest ListNotificationRoutesResponse

List the owner/team routing rules. A route selects extra channels for the events whose in-app audience matches it.
GetNotificationRoute GetNotificationRouteRequest NotificationRoute

Read one routing rule.
CreateNotificationRoute CreateNotificationRouteRequest NotificationRoute

Create one routing rule.
UpdateNotificationRoute UpdateNotificationRouteRequest NotificationRoute

Update one routing rule: a masked update, or a full update of its mutable fields when the mask is empty.
DeleteNotificationRoute DeleteNotificationRouteRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

Delete one routing rule.

OAuthAuthorizationRequest

OAuthAuthorizationRequest is one pending OAuth 2.1 authorization request. It

is display-only: the server trusts nothing the consent page sends back except

the approve decision, and never exposes the authorization code, the PKCE

challenge or the client's polling state here.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
name string

Format: oauthAuthorizationRequests/{request_id}

client_name string

The client's self-reported name, as registered. It is not verified: it is shown so the user can tell clients apart, not relied upon.

redirect_uri string

Where the authorization code will be delivered. Shown in full so the user can recognise a redirect they did not expect.

resource string

The resource the client asked for, which must be this deployment's MCP endpoint.

scopes string repeated

The scopes the client asked for.

create_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

expire_time google.protobuf.Timestamp

request_ip string

The source address the request came from, as the server sees it (it follows the trusted-proxy rules).

OAuthService

OAuthService serves the browser-facing half of the OAuth 2.1 authorization

server. The protocol endpoints themselves -- /oauth/authorize,

/oauth/authorize/complete, /oauth/token and /oauth/register -- are plain HTTP,

because OAuth clients do not speak ConnectRPC; this service carries only what

the SPA consent page needs.

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
GetOAuthAuthorizationRequest GetOAuthAuthorizationRequestRequest OAuthAuthorizationRequest

GetOAuthAuthorizationRequest returns one pending authorization request so the consent page can show what is being approved. The caller must be signed in; the request carries no permission annotation, like the device login confirmation it mirrors. Permissions required: None
ApproveOAuthAuthorizationRequest ApproveOAuthAuthorizationRequestRequest .google.protobuf.Empty

ApproveOAuthAuthorizationRequest records the signed-in user's decision. The approver becomes the identity the access token will be issued for. The browser then goes to /oauth/authorize/complete, which mints the authorization code and redirects it to the client, so the code never passes through an RPC response or through the page's own JavaScript. Permissions required: None

Top

DataQualitySetting

DataQualitySetting configures the data quality subsystem for the workspace.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
enable_llm_analysis bool

Whether the LLM-assisted entries (rule draft, failure explanation, column labels) are enabled. Off by default: the rule engine is fully offline.

llm_provider_profile string

The LLM provider profile the quality analyses use, as a profile resource name. Empty means the first allowed profile.

store_failure_samples bool

Whether failed checks keep the sampled rows as evidence. Off means a result records its counts but no values.

failure_sample_limit int32

How many failed rows a result keeps. Zero means the server default (20); capped at 100.

default_schedule_interval google.protobuf.Duration

The schedule interval a target starts with when it gets its first rule. Zero means the server default (one hour). Existing targets keep their own schedule.

daily_execution_limit int32

The workspace's daily execution ceiling; 0 means the server default (10000).

daily_column_analysis_limit int32

The workspace's daily column-analysis ceiling; 0 means the server default.

max_columns_per_analysis int32

The maximum number of columns one analysis may cover; 0 means the server default (50).

send_sample_values_to_llm bool

Whether raw sample values may be sent to the LLM. Off by default: only aggregate profiles leave the deployment.

daily_llm_analysis_limit int32

The workspace's daily L1+L2 LLM analysis ceiling (rule drafts and failure explanations). Zero means the server default (10000); capped at 1000000.

llm_concurrency_limit int32

How many data quality LLM analyses may run at once in this process. Zero means the server default (8); accepted range 1-64.

weekly_digest QualityDigestSetting

The weekly data quality digest. The digest is one workspace-level summary delivered through the outbound channels that name NOTIFICATION_TYPE_DATA_QUALITY_DIGEST explicitly; it has no per-recipient inbox copy. A data_quality update that omits this nested message keeps the stored schedule (so a client that predates the digest cannot clear it); sending the message explicitly replaces it, including with enabled=false.

time_zone string

The IANA time zone (for example "Asia/Shanghai") the time variables of check filters and custom SQL are resolved in: ${today}, ${yesterday} and the ${now} family. Empty means UTC. It does not affect a check's schedule, which belongs to the target.

agent_autonomy_enabled bool

Whether the workspace's agent principals may write plan declarations and proposed change requests. Off by default: turning it off is the kill switch that returns the workspace to human-only edits.

EmailSetting

EmailSetting configures the SMTP server workspace notifications are emailed

through. There is one per workspace: a channel of kind EMAIL delivers through

it, and an email channel fails while it is unset.

FieldTypeLabelDescription

The From address. It must be an address the SMTP server is allowed to send as. Empty means email delivery is not configured.

from_name string

The display name shown beside the From address.

smtp SMTPConfig

The SMTP server.

password_set bool

Whether a password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

timezone string

The IANA time zone the windows are evaluated in, for example "Asia/Shanghai". Required while enabled.

windows QuietWindow repeated

Recurring weekly windows. At least one window or maintenance window is required while enabled.

maintenance_windows MaintenanceWindow repeated

One-off absolute windows for planned maintenance. A window whose end has passed is inert and can be removed.

QuietWindow

QuietWindow is one recurring weekly quiet window.

FieldTypeLabelDescription
days DayOfWeek repeated

The days the window starts on. A window whose end is at or before its start crosses midnight into the following day.

start string

"HH:MM" in the setting's time zone.

end string

"HH:MM" in the setting's time zone.

WorkspaceProfileSetting

FieldTypeLabelDescription
external_url string

The external URL used for the SSO authentication callback.

disallow_signup bool

Disallow self-service signup. When enabled, only a workspace admin can create users.

disallow_password_signin bool

Disallow password signin. Workspace admins are exempt.

openlineage_retention_days int32

The number of days persisted OpenLineage runs are kept. Zero (the default) keeps them forever.

domains string repeated

The email domains (for example "example.com") whose users may sign up and sign in. Only enforced when enforce_identity_domain is on; an empty list disables the restriction.

enforce_identity_domain bool

Whether to restrict signup and signin to the domains above.

allowed_llm_provider_profiles string repeated

The LLM provider profiles ExplainSQL may use, as profile resource names ("llm-provider-profiles/{id}"). Empty means every enabled profile is allowed.

mcp_enabled bool

Whether the MCP endpoint and its OAuth 2.1 authorization server are served. Off by default, and only usable once external_url is configured.

sso_email_identity_idps string repeated

The identity providers, as idps/{idp} resource names, whose email claim may stand in for a stable subject. For a listed provider, field_mapping.subject becomes optional and a login whose address claim matches an existing account makes that account reachable through the provider — adopting it (its password is replaced with a random one) when it had no provider binding at all. Empty (the default) turns the feature off for every provider. The address claim is mutable, so listing a provider asserts that it verifies addresses and that its configuration, which only an administrator can write, is trusted: whoever can set an address there can sign in as the account it names.

data_quality DataQualitySetting

Data quality settings. They are read by the quality subsystem and written on the data quality settings page; every zero value means the server's default, which is why the reader resolves defaults instead of trusting the wire value.

DayOfWeek

DayOfWeek is an ISO 8601 weekday: 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday.

NameNumberDescription
DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED 0

DAY_OF_WEEK_MONDAY 1

DAY_OF_WEEK_TUESDAY 2

DAY_OF_WEEK_WEDNESDAY 3

DAY_OF_WEEK_THURSDAY 4

DAY_OF_WEEK_FRIDAY 5

DAY_OF_WEEK_SATURDAY 6

DAY_OF_WEEK_SUNDAY 7

SMTPAuthentication

SMTPAuthentication is the login mechanism of the SMTP connection.

NameNumberDescription
SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_UNSPECIFIED 0

SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_NONE 1

No login; only for a server that accepts mail from trusted hosts.
SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_PLAIN 2

SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_LOGIN 3

SMTP_AUTHENTICATION_CRAM_MD5 4

SMTPEncryption

SMTPEncryption is the transport security of the SMTP connection.

NameNumberDescription
SMTP_ENCRYPTION_UNSPECIFIED 0

SMTP_ENCRYPTION_NONE 1

No transport encryption. Only for a server on a trusted network.
SMTP_ENCRYPTION_STARTTLS 2

Upgrade the connection with STARTTLS after the greeting.
SMTP_ENCRYPTION_SSL_TLS 3

Implicit TLS from the first byte, usually port 465.

SettingService

Method NameRequest TypeResponse TypeDescription
GetWorkspaceProfileSetting GetWorkspaceProfileSettingRequest WorkspaceProfileSetting

Get the workspace profile setting. Permissions required: None This method is readable without credentials because the login page needs to know whether self-service signup is enabled.
UpdateWorkspaceProfileSetting UpdateWorkspaceProfileSettingRequest WorkspaceProfileSetting

Update the workspace profile setting.
GetDebugConfig GetDebugConfigRequest GetDebugConfigResponse

Get the workspace runtime debug config.
UpdateDebugConfig UpdateDebugConfigRequest UpdateDebugConfigResponse

Update the workspace runtime debug config. Enabling it switches the process-wide log level to debug, gates the verbose request logging emitted by the debug interceptor, exposes /debug/pprof, and allows panic handlers to return stack traces to the caller. Disabling it restores info-level logging and generic panic errors.
GetEmailSetting GetEmailSettingRequest EmailSetting

Get the workspace email setting. It is returned empty when email delivery is not configured, so the settings page can render one form either way.
UpdateEmailSetting UpdateEmailSettingRequest EmailSetting

Update the workspace email setting. The password is write-only: an empty one on update keeps the stored password, and no read returns it.
SendTestEmail SendTestEmailRequest SendTestEmailResponse

Send a test email to the caller's own address through the configured SMTP server. It is not audited: it changes nothing, and it is a diagnostic probe the settings page can repeat while an administrator types the server in.
GetQuietHoursSetting GetQuietHoursSettingRequest QuietHoursSetting

Get the workspace quiet-hours schedule for outbound notifications.
UpdateQuietHoursSetting UpdateQuietHoursSettingRequest QuietHoursSetting

Update the workspace quiet-hours schedule. Any update releases the deliveries the previous schedule was holding, so shortening or disabling it takes effect immediately; held rows are then re-evaluated by the next dispatcher tick.
